body.translated_text: <s>Tathāgatabimbakārāpaṇasūtra</s> (Sūtra on the Making of Images of the Tathāgata)

children.text:
) s sakotūhalahṛdayā evam ūcu |
aho puṇyaphalaprabhāvam iti mahātvaṃ
aho puṇyaprabhāvam iti tūṣṇībabhūvuḥ
  tataḥ su
children.translated_text: ) With hearts full of wonder, they spoke thus: "Oh, the greatness of the power of the fruit of merit!" "Oh, the power of merit!" — and they fell silent. Then <s>Su</s>-

children.text: ) saparivāra bhagavantaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya śirasā praṇamya bhagavato 'ntikaṃ niṣaṇṇa dharmaśravaṇārtham* a
children.translated_text: ) together with his retinue, having circumambulated the Blessed One and bowed his head, sat near the Blessed One for the purpose of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: ) bhagavāṃ sarvasatvānusaṃśayaṃ jñātvā tebhyo mahājanakāyebhya dharmaśrāvaṇikebhyaḥ tasya suvarṇaprabhasya rājakumārasya pū
children.translated_text: ) the Blessed One, knowing the doubts of all beings, for those great assemblies desirous of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, [taught] concerning that prince <s>Suvarṇaprabha</s>'s former

) a <s>Dharma</s>-teaching that was the cause for displaying the arising of [his] power and glory, of various kinds, connected with <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) and the Four Noble Truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>),

children.text: ) dharmadeśanāṃ deśayati | ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇaṃ svarthaṃ suvyaṃjanaṃ kevalaṃ pa
children.translated_text: ) He taught the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching: good in the beginning, good in the middle, good at the end, with good meaning, with good phrasing, complete,

children.text:
) pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ prakāśayati sma :
  bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavaḥ atīte 'dhvani ekanavatime kalpe (
children.translated_text:
) pure and stainless. He proclaimed the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>):
"Once upon a time, O monks, in the past, in the ninety-first <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age), (

children.text: ) vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannas sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiś śāstā devamanuṣyā
children.translated_text: ) there was a Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Vipaśyī</s>, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans,

children.text: ) buddho bhagavāṃ buddhakṛtyam a..aśiṣyavineyakṛtyaṃ kṛtvā nirindhano 'gnir iva parinirvṛta samabhijagāma : tad eka pu
children.translated_text: ) <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. Having accomplished the Buddha's task and the task of training disciples, he passed into complete <s>parinirvāṇa</s> like a fire whose fuel is exhausted. Then one

children.text: ) bhikṣavaḥ paruṣadaridrakṛṣikarmaṇāvaprativṛtti bhagavatā vipaśyina śāsanebhiḥ prasannāḥ bhagavato vipa
children.translated_text: ) O monks, a rough, poor farmer by occupation, having gained faith in the teachings of the Blessed One <s>Vipaśyī</s>, [wished to] make an image of the Blessed <s>Vipa</s>-

children.text:
) pratimāṃ kartā
  tasmiṃ kāle tasmiṃ samaye sa evāyaṃ suvarṇaprabho rājakumāra yad bhagavato vipaśyinaḥ prati
children.translated_text: ) At that time, at that moment, this very prince <s>Suvarṇaprabha</s> was the one who had an image of the Blessed <s>Vipaśyī</s>
) By the power of the arising of the meritorious fruit [of that deed], he experienced the greatness of divine pleasures, enjoyments, and sovereignty.

children.text:
) rājakumāra samāsato bhikṣava sarvāsu jātiṣu tad bhāṣayāmi:
  saptaratnamayena samanvāgato śrī
children.translated_text:
) prince, in brief, O monks, in all his births — I shall speak of them:
Endowed with the seven treasures, [he attained] the glorious
) lord of the four continents, traverser of the sky, with unobstructed movement of the jewel-wheel, supreme overlord.

children.text:
) caturdvīpeśvaro rājā cakravartī babhūvu |
  anenaiva buddhapratimāpuṇyaphalavipākena tathaivaṃvidha | (
children.translated_text:
) he became a <s>Cakravartī</s> king, lord of the four continents.
By this very ripening of the meritorious fruit of making a Buddha image, in the same manner, (

children.text: ) sa kāmāvacareṣu devanikāyeṣu svargeṣu ekaikaśaḥ śatasahasrakṛtvā bhikṣava devānām indro rājā babhūva : (
children.translated_text: ) in the heavens of the desire-realm gods, in each [heaven] individually, a hundred thousand times, O monks, he became <s>Indra</s>, king of the gods.

children.text: ) evaṃvidha : śatasahasrakṛtvā daśa brahmakāyikeṣu brahmādhipatir babhūvu: anulomapratilomaja
children.translated_text: ) In the same manner, a hundred thousand times he became the chief of <s>Brahmā</s> in the ten <s>Brahmakāyika</s> [heavens]. In a hundred thousand births, both in forward and reverse order,

children.text: ) koṭi kṣatriyabrāhmaṇeśvarādhipatikuleṣu rājā babhūva | evaṃvidhaś ca bhikṣava| sau
children.translated_text: ) he became king in tens of millions of ruling families of <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and lords. And in this manner, O monks,
with beauty, grace, splendor, fame, glory, and strength, (

children.text: ) svargā cyuta| aiśvaryeṣu rājakule jātaḥ uttamajāta anuttamajā
children.translated_text: ) having fallen from heaven, born in a royal family of sovereignty, of the highest birth, of unsurpassed birth,

children.text: ) suvarṇaprabho rājakumāraḥ antike devamanuṣyāṇāṃ acyutaṃ ajaraṃ amaraṇaṃ śivaṃ śāntaṃ padaṃ labhiṣyatīti | tato (
children.translated_text: ) prince <s>Suvarṇaprabha</s> will attain, in the presence of gods and humans, the imperishable, unaging, deathless, auspicious, peaceful state." Then, (

children.text: ) 'sya bhikṣava suvarṇaprabhasya rājakumārasya buddhapratimāpuṇyaphalaprabhāvam anuśṛṇutā mānuṣyajātiṣu ye
children.translated_text: ) "O monks, hearing of the power of the meritorious fruit of making a Buddha image of this prince <s>Suvarṇaprabha</s>, in [your] human births,

children.text:
) ātmahitaparahitakāmena nāma bhikṣava buddhapratimā nikaraṇīyā |
  tadyathā bhikṣava : mṛnmayī vā | (
children.translated_text:
) desire their own welfare and the welfare of others should indeed, O monks, make Buddha images.
Namely, O monks: of clay, (

children.text: ) śailamayī vā | dantamayī vā | dārumayī vā | suvarṇamayī vā | kaṃsamayī vā | tra...mayī vā | rupyamayī (
children.translated_text: ) or of stone, or of ivory, or of wood, or of gold, or of bronze, or of [...] material, or of silver, (

children.text: ) vā sphaṭikamayī vā | maṇiratnakamayī vā | rītamayī vā | buddhapratimā karaṇīyakā vā | dīrghakā vā | hra
children.translated_text: ) or of crystal, or of jewels and gems, or of brass — a Buddha image should be made, whether large, whether

children.text:
) vā | sadhātukaṃ vā | sapratītyasamutpādaṃ vā |
  buddhapratimā kārayitvā | sthāpayitvā gandhodakapuṣpodakādibhi
children.translated_text:
) or [medium], with relics (<s>dhātu</s>) or with [an inscription of] <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination).
Having made and installed a Buddha image, with fragrant water, flower-water, and other

children.text: ) pūjāviśeṣai| snāpayitvā pūjayitvā yasya kasyacid bhikṣavaḥ kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā buddhapratimāpu
children.translated_text: ) special offerings, having bathed and worshipped [it] — for any son of good family or daughter of good family, O monks, the outflow of merit from the Buddha image,

children.text:
) puṇyaskandhaḥ puṇyarāśi aprameya asādharaṇa: anantyupama: puṇyaskandheti
  punar aparaṃ bhikṣava: (
children.translated_text:
) the mass of merit, the heap of merit, is immeasurable, extraordinary, infinite, incomparable — such a mass of merit!"
"Furthermore, O monks, (

children.text: ) yaḥ kaścid bhikṣur vā bhikṣuṇī vā upāsako vā upāsikā vā | kṣatriyo vā brāhmaṇo vā | vaiśyo vā | śūdro vā evaṃrūpā
children.translated_text: ) whatever monk or nun, male or female lay follower, <s>Kṣatriya</s> or <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s> or <s>Śūdra</s> — in such

children.text: ) jātiṣu | śrutidharo bhavati | jātismaro bhavati | svajanaparijanadāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaprabhṛtiṣu sa ādeyavādyo bhavati | (
children.translated_text: ) births — one becomes a retainer of what is heard, one becomes a rememberer of past lives, among one's own people, relatives, servants, workers, and attendants, one becomes one whose words are authoritative. (

children.text: ) sarvasatvapriyadarśanadharo bhavati | sarvaguṇalakṣaṇadharo bhavati sarvasatvādhipatir bhavati | sarvabuddhapratyekabuddhaśrāvakārhadguṇa
children.translated_text: ) One becomes pleasing to the sight of all beings, one becomes endowed with all virtues and auspicious marks, one becomes the lord of all beings, one becomes endowed with all the qualities

children.text: ) bhavati | nityaṃ bodhicittaparāyaṇo bhavati | yasya yatrābhikāṃkṣati | tatra tatra etaṃ labhati | rāgadveṣamoherṣyāmātsarya
children.translated_text: ) One is always devoted to <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). Whatever one desires, wherever — there one obtains it. From desire, hatred, delusion, envy, jealousy,

children.text: ) vivarjito bhavati | buddhatvam anvantaram adhigacchati | kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāṇaṃ śāntam adhigacchatīti vadāmi bhikṣavaḥ (
children.translated_text: ) one becomes free. One attains <s>Buddhahood</s> without interval. And one quickly attains the peaceful <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — thus I say, O monks."

)
  tat kasmād dhetor anantaphalasamudayaprabhāva | buddhapratimāpuṇyaphalasamudayaprabhāvam* buddhapratimāpuṇyaphalavipāka (
children.translated_text: "And why? Because of the power of the arising of infinite fruit — the power of the arising of the meritorious fruit of a Buddha image, the ripening of the meritorious fruit of a Buddha image.

children.text:
)
  parinirvṛto 'pi adhigato nāpi buddho bhagavāṃ parinirvṛta iva buddhapratimāyā darśanād iti vadāmi bhikṣava idam avocad bhagavāṃ (
children.translated_text: Even though the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, has not [truly] attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — [he is still present] through the seeing of a Buddha image. Thus I say, O monks." This the Blessed One spoke. (

) Then he further spoke these verses:
"Having formerly made an excellent image of [the Buddha] <s>Kāśyapa</s>, and having bathed [it] with fragrant waters, the foremost among the twice-born —
) with flowers, sweet fragrances, and delightful

children.text:
tenaiva puṇyena bhavād vimuktaḥ 1
  yaṃ nirmalaḥ kleśamalair vimukta cittasya citteśvaratāgatiṃ syaḥ
  rūpaṃ na tṛptāś ca nirīkṣya matvā tadbiṃba saṃ
children.translated_text:
by that very merit was freed from [the cycle of] existence. (1)
He who is stainless, freed from the defilements of the <s>kleśas</s>, to attain the state of mastery over mind — [his] form, even after seeing [it], one is not satiated — [therefore] one should bathe the image

)
Various enjoyments of many kinds, with splendor surpassing the beauty of the moon, sun, and gentleness — women and men in this world obtain [these]

)
With minds freed from the darkness of the <s>kleśas</s>, like the full moon [dispelling] the darkness of delusion, men and women attain the peaceful state
by bathing the image of the <s>Jina</s>.

The image of him whose fame [pervades] the three worlds, the mighty one of the ten powers, whose renown is celebrated in all directions —

obtain in heaven and in their own realm a form that delights the eyes, pure as fine gold. They who desire peace

Having heard this and other such well-connected <s>Dharma</s>-teachings concerning <s>Suvarṇaprabha</s>, the five hundred
) [women of the] inner palace, the beloved retinue, and prince <s>Suvarṇaprabha</s>, [experiencing] the joy and happiness arising from the royal glory of the meritorious fruit of the Buddha image,

children.text:
) sarvaṃ gārhasthyam apahāya tathaiva śāsane pravrajita
  yoniśa sa manaskāraṃ kṛtvā sarvakleśaprahāṇā arhatvaṃ strīpa
children.translated_text: ) abandoned all household life entirely and likewise went forth into the [Buddha's] teaching. Having applied proper mental attention (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>), through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>, [they attained] <s>Arhatship</s> — the women

children.text: ) samaloṣṭakāṃcana samacittāḥ kṛtaṃ karaṇīyā apahṛtabhārāḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojana vimuktās saṃsārabandha
children.translated_text: who regard a clod of earth and gold equally, whose minds are even, whose task is accomplished, whose burdens are removed, whose fetters of existence (<s>bhavasaṃyojana</s>) are utterly destroyed, who are liberated from the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s>
whose pair of feet are venerated by all the gods, fully awakened — [this is] the illumination of the greatness and glory of the accumulation of the meritorious fruits of <s>Buddha</s> images

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandam* bhikṣavaś caturdiśasaṃkhyārhatvaṃ babhūvu |
children.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavān</s>). Those <s>bhikṣus</s>, with uplifted minds, rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One. And the <s>bhikṣus</s> of the four directions attained <s>arhatship</s> (<s>arhatva</s>).
This sūtra illuminating the meritorious fruits of <s>Buddha</s> images is completed.

body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgatbimbakārāpaṇa Sūtra</s> (Sūtra on the Commissioning of Images of the <s>Tathāgata</s>) is completed.
